newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey busts anti-rebel crime gang in southeast.
newsitem.headline: Turkey busts anti-rebel crime gang in southeast.

text.p: Police have arrested members of the anti-guerrilla forces in the mainly Kurdish southeast of Turkey who abused their positions to carry out a string of serious crimes, Anatolian news agency said on Thursday.
It said four special forces policemen and members of a state-paid village militia were part of a 16-strong gang that kidnapped a man in the remote province of Hakkari last week.
Anatolian said masked and armed members of the gang posed as Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas to kidnap the man, named as Necip Baskin, and demand a ransom of 200,000 German marks ($131,450).
Gendarmerie police later rescued the victim and arrested the gang which confessed to the abduction and many other crimes, which the agency did not specify.
Human rights activists have often accused police crack teams and village guards of rights abuses and involvement in common crime amid a bitter political conflict.
More than 20,000 people have died in 12 years of clashes between the security forces and the rebels, fighting for self-rule.
Around 60,000 village guards, mostly Kurds, are paid and armed by the state to fight the guerrillas.
